conventions_learned: Door = INSERT of block D<w>W<t>. D10W12 = 1.00 m door (the 10 is in decimetres) in a 0.12 wall. D80W12 = 0.80, D90W12 = 0.90, D90W25 = 0.90 in a 0.25 wall (stair door). The width from the name always equals the distance between the two jamb lines in the block geometry.
Use: D10W12 = office doors onto the corridor and the accessible WC. D80W12 = WCs and the FTR room. D90W12 = IT, electric and DAS/GSM rooms. D90W25 = stair.

Door blocks are inserted on layer W OR layer PR, often mirrored (xscale=-1) and rotated 0/90/180/270. Never use the insert layer or the insert angle to read them. Push the block's jamb lines and leaf arc through ins.matrix44() instead.
In D10W12 the opening runs along the block's y axis, but in D80/D90 it runs along x.

Mirrored block ARC/LWPOLYLINE entities have extrusion (0,0,-1), so they are in OCS coordinates. Read them with ezdxf.path.make_path, not the raw center/get_points. render_floor._segments gets this wrong for mirrored door arcs; I left it unedited as instructed.
There are no double doors and no sliding doors on any floor. All doors are single swing.
Not doors or windows: LP on W (7 per floor) = level-mark symbol; WB/P on FUR = basin/WC; ST-2 on PR1 = stair arrow; raw PR lines = stair handrails and lift cars.

The 18 random-name INSERTs on W per floor ('rt5hrt6', '56y', ...) are axis tags: a CI circle plus a TEXT-DIM letter (ز ا ب ج د / 1 2 3 4 after SOSA decode). Their insert points lie far away, so floor_entities skips them. This explains '37 INSERT on W' = 6+3+3 door blocks + 7 LP + 18 tags.
Random-name blocks on layer X = axis bubbles.

F02 only: 4 door leaves drawn without a block on WIN (arc r≈1.0 + leaf line). Two are east terrace doors inside glazed assemblies. Two are corner doors cutting the curved glazing; those sit in glazing, not masonry. F02 also has two W circles (r 0.375 / 0.275) that are round elements, not doors.
WIN layer: only CONTINUOUS lines are glazing. DASHED WIN lines (x=0.27 west, y=39.35 north, y=-1.42 south) are projection or cladding lines outside the facade.
A window = 2 parallel WIN lines 0.12-0.15 apart inside a 0.25 wall. Width = the span common to both lines; one frame line is sometimes drawn ~7 cm longer.
West facade: 13.00 m curtain wall with no masonry. NW/SW corners: curved glazing, concentric arcs r 1.95/2.07, length 3.16 m (3.28 m at NW on F05-F08).
Every continuous WIN line and arc on every floor is explained (window, frame piece or door leaf). No orphans.

F02 east facade: the masonry openings 2.35 and 1.35 (the same as the windows on the other floors) are filled with assemblies. 2.35 = 0.10 frame + door 1.00 + fixed glass 1.25. 1.35 = 0.15 + door 1.00 + 0.20. The masonry deduction is the whole opening, not the sum of the products.

Architect DIMs (layer DIM, style WWW) never measure an interior door: no DIM defpoint touches any door jamb. Interior DIMs are room and corridor widths. Facade DIM chains measure windows, and 20/24 masonry windows plus the curtain wall have a matching DIM with no mismatch.

A face is counted as covered when it lies between two W lines no more than 0.66 m apart running away from it, or inside another element or a shaft. It does not separate facade (external) faces from internal ones, and it does not deduct door frames that sit on a column face.

conventions_learned: All walls are drawn as two face lines on W with no centre-lines, and columns/cores (Etabs-col/COL) cut the walls. Rooms are read straight from the faces: buffer every primitive by 1.5 cm, take the free faces of the union, then grow them back 1.5 cm with mitre joins so the polygon sits exactly on the drawn faces.

Door gaps are left open in the wall drawing (the D<w>W<t> block holds only the leaf and arc). To close a room you add a quad between the two jambs from openings.py. Door-less openings (lift landings 2x1.25, the 0.80 opening between offices 3 and 2 on F03/F04) are closed with a rectangle across the wall.

WIN glazing is two lines (frame 12-15 cm deep). The room stops at the inner glazing line, and the band between the two lines counts as wall body. DASHED WIN lines are projection/cladding lines, not boundaries.
Hatched (ANSI31) 'try' boxes are solid masonry fins at the 13 m west curtain wall. Un-hatched 'try' boxes with an X are shafts (14 per floor, 0.24-1.37 m2), often sitting inside WC walls.

MASS lines inside a stair are the stair well (ignored). A MASS LWPOLYLINE with 20 or more vertices is the slab edge (F02 terraces/planters). Other MASS lines are the lift-front wall and terrace parapets.
Arabic SHX labels (style ARA) run LEFTWARDS from their insertion point and Latin labels (-A-TEXT) run rightwards. Labels sitting in a wall body snap to the nearest face within 1.2 m.

'حمام' + 'ذوي الهمم' in one space = one accessible WC. 'المصاعد الادارية فقط' is a sign, not a room name. The SE WC (2.63 m2) has no label on any floor and is named from the WC pan block P (FUR). F02 has no 'ممر' label.

The corridor and the lift lobby are one open space with no wall between them. It is split by a virtual 7.12 m chord that continues the corridor wall face (identical on all floors). The chord must never be plastered or counted as masonry.
The lift core = 1 space of 6.90 m2 holding 2 cars (two X marks on PR).

Open-air spaces (terraces 'تراس سماوي', planters 'زرع') exist on F02 only, 58.15 m2 in total. They have no ceiling, and the wall faces towards them take external plaster. An unlabelled F02 planter is recognised from the AR-CONC hatch on W.

import sys; sys.path.insert(0, 'tools'); from rooms import analyze_floor, run, to_json, render
res = analyze_floor(n)   # n = 2..8 or a Floor object; options use_cache=True, refresh_openings=False

res['rooms'] is a list of dicts. Each has:
  id ('F03-R07'), name (decoded Arabic/English), category (office|wc|corridor|lobby|service|stair|lift|shaft|terrace|planter|void), category_ar, open_air, indoor
  area (m2 net), perimeter (all rings, inner face), perimeter_outer, n_holes
  boundary {wall, column, glazing, door, opening, shaft, solid_try, slab_edge, mass, extension, virtual, unresolved}: lengths in m by what bounds the room
  doors[] / openings[] / windows[]: ids from openings.py; windows_partial_m {id: facing m} when the room faces only part of a window
  labels[], flags[], centroid, bbox, inscribed_r, n_cars (lift), wc_pans
  dim_checks[{dim, value, room_width, diff, status ok|jog|mismatch, lateral, p2, p3}]
  _poly: shapely Polygon in local coordinates (not in the JSON)

res['totals'] holds: by_category{cat:{name_ar,n,area,perimeter}}, n_rooms, net_indoor_area, net_usable_area, ceiling_area, open_air_area, gross_floor_area, gross_outline_perimeter, walls_columns_area, boundary_by_kind_indoor, boundary_by_kind_open_air, footprint_bbox.

res['checks'] holds: labels_unplaced, office_numbers, offices_missing, duplicate_names, rooms_flagged, extensions, corridor_lobby_splits, closed_pockets_as_solid, doors_not_two_sided, windows_unassigned, dims_ok, dims_jog, dims_mismatch.

Private keys (not in the JSON): res['_P'] = tagged boundary primitives [(geom, kind, ref)], res['_footprint'] = gross outline Polygon, res['_wall_bodies'].

to_json(res) strips the '_' keys. render(res, png, zoom=(x0,y0,x1,y1)) draws the review image.

CLI: python tools/rooms.py [floors...] [--no-png] [--zoom X0 Y0 X1 Y1] [--no-cache] [--refresh-openings]. It writes output/rooms/F0x.json, F0x.png, F0x_south.png, F0x_north.png and summary.json; running a subset of floors updates only their entries in summary.json.

defects.description: windows_partial_m over-counts the facing length of shared windows. windows_on() measures seg ∩ poly.buffer(0.32), and that buffer reaches 0.32 m past each end of the room along the window. The per-room partial lengths of one window therefore add up to more than the window itself. Findings doc §7 presents these numbers as the per-office split of the curtain wall and of W26. A plaster or opening tool that deducts windows per room from this field would deduct about 1.2 m × height too much per floor at the west curtain wall.
